reviewer: Codex, personal complete-final-answer read; no paid judge
primary_route: Yeast-juice fractionation, chemical add-back and heat-dependent functional reconstitution.

checks.quote: # Proposed Protocol: Testing the Requirement for a Heat-Stable, Separable Factor in Yeast-Juice Fermentation
checks.reason: No proposal to consult prior Methods, supplements or validated protocols and verify detailed-condition transfer before execution.
Heat-killed source may retain heat-stable factor; no active-F rescue excludes inhibitors in treated/stored inactive matrices.

checks.quote: removes filtrate water/ion contribution while retaining solutes
checks.reason: Dialysis can remove the small organic factor with salts; lyophilization cannot selectively recover lost solutes. Claimed retention requires recovery validation.
Changing R input to match total protein changes enzyme dose. Hold R fixed and balance other protein; also no post-heat evaporation correction.
Precision duplicates do not calibrate gas/product accuracy, recovery or leakage.
No fixed product amount/volume convention, blank correction and weak/missing reporting.
Fixed count lacks variance/precision/power justification; initial single large source limits biological replication.
Integrity stop includes deliberately denatured protein controls, invalidating expected control behavior.
Model/multiplicity specified but effect CIs and heat/negative equivalence analysis absent.
Conductivity does not establish matching of individual ions.
No refreeze and fresh independent confirmation.
Boiled R rescue does not refute heat stability: it may release residual bound heat-stable factor. Decision is non-identifying.
Both routes use size-selective membranes; no different principle or validated independent product assay.
No linked raw-file/unit manifest and exact analysis versions/settings.
